verdict_reason: The attribution defect is closed and I verified both halves. (a) Ma et al. 2018 Eq. (4), fetched from the paper, is LID_hat(x) = -( (1/k) sum_{i=1..k} log(r_i(x)/r_k(x)) )^{-1}; lid.py computes -k / sum log(r_i/r_k), which is algebraically identical, and the class docstring now names Ma et al. Eq. (4) and states the offsets. I confirmed the offsets numerically on 200 queries: implemented/Levina-Bickel(k-1) = 1.0526315789 against the exact k/(k-1) = 1.0526315789 (+5.2632%), and implemented/(k-2) = 1.1111111111 against k/(k-2) (+11.1111%) -- the docstring's two figures are exactly right. (b) The kernel itself is exact: on 500 real gpt2 last-layer states BLME's lid_mean is 7.6278910655 against an exact float64 brute force at 7.6278910655 (rel 0.000e+00) and the official mle_batch at 7.6278910655 (rel 1.16e-16) on the same query population. Analytic anchors: uniform in a d-ball at N=5000, k=20, lid_median 2.0951 / 5.0415 / 9.5551 / 16.3202 for true d = 2 / 5 / 10 / 20.
comparable_reason: Distance-based local dimension is ambient-dimension invariant and I re-verified that exactly: zero-padding a d=64 cloud into ambient 64 / 256 / 2048 leaves lid_mean at 37.3762056471 in all three cases, bit-identical. So it is not an arithmetic width readout. But it is empirically size-associated across the 61-model archive: lid_mean Spearman +0.516 with d_model, +0.431 with n_layers, +0.420 with log(params), -0.226 with vocab, over an archived range 13.32-35.56. Separately the fixed-k estimator truncates at high true dimension -- d-ball medians 2.0951 (+4.8%), 5.0415 (+0.8%), 9.5551 (-4.4%), 16.3202 (-18.4%) for d = 2/5/10/20 -- so the compression is itself dimension-dependent. Comparable only after residualising on d_model, and with the truncation stated.
normalized_variant: lid_mean_scalenorm (= lid_mean / log(d_model); NORMALIZERS in src/blme/normalization.py)
github_reason: Ran the authors' mle_batch from xingjunm/lid_adversarial_subspace_detection (util.py) verbatim -- k=min(k,len(data)-1); f = lambda v: -k/np.sum(np.log(v/v[-1])); cdist -> sort -> [:,1:k+1] -- head-to-head against BLME on 500 real gpt2 float32 last-layer states at k=20. Official 7.6278910655 vs BLME 7.6278910655, rel 1.16e-16, on the identical 495-query population; against an exact float64 brute force the relative error is 0.000e+00. The one population deviation: the official code returns 0.0 for a query with an exact duplicate and KEEPS it, so its unfiltered mean over all 500 queries is 7.5516121548 against BLME's 7.6278910655 (+1.01%), 5 of 500 queries being exact duplicates on this corpus. I also re-checked the standing codex RED (a float32 (100,512) cloud offset to 1e5 allegedly giving 41.964 vs 57.757): it does not reproduce -- the Gram-select / exact-refine kernel returns rel 0.000e+00 against float64 at every offset up to 1e6.
paper_reason: Confirmed against the paper text: Ma et al. publish detector AUCs (Tables 1-3), a schematic Fig. 1 carrying two illustrative values (LID 1.53 for a normal sample, 4.36 for an adversarial one) with no released coordinates, and Fig. 2 LID distributions min-max normalised to [0,1], which destroys the raw scale. There is no reproducible published raw-LID number. The available anchor is analytic: for points uniform in a d-ball the true LID is d, and BLME (k=20, N=5000) returns lid_median 2.0951, 5.0415, 9.5551, 16.3202 for d = 2, 5, 10, 20.
confounds_reason: Over 61 archived models (d 512-7168, L 6-64, V 32k-262k, 70M-34B): lid_mean rho = +0.516 (d_model), +0.431 (n_layers), -0.226 (vocab), +0.420 (log params); lid_median +0.496 / +0.419 / -0.297 / +0.416. Real, but NOT mechanically forced -- the zero-padding test gives bit-identical lid_mean = 37.3762056471 at ambient 64, 256 and 2048, so ambient width enters only through the data, and _meta_num_estimates is flat (495 of 500 on gpt2). Note the obvious correction OVER-corrects: lid_mean/sqrt(d_model) flips to rho = -0.735 with d_model, so a sqrt(d) twin would be worse than the raw value. Residualise, do not rescale.
defects: CODE: duplicate queries are dropped rather than retained. The reference mle_batch returns 0.0 for a query with an exact duplicate and keeps it; BLME returns 0.0 and then removes it at the `lid > 0` filter, so duplicate frequency silently changes both the estimand and _meta_num_estimates. Measured on the shipped path (gpt2, num_samples=50 -> 500 points): 5 of 500 queries dropped, BLME 7.6279 against the reference's 7.5516 over all 500, a model-dependent +1.01%. On a duplicate-heavy cloud the gap reaches 2x. The policy is defensible (Eq. 4 is undefined at r_1 = 0) but it is undeclared outside a _meta_ key.
CODE: an all-duplicate cloud makes _compute_lid_for_matrix return None and the task return an error dict; the reference returns an array. Fails closed rather than degrading.

CODE: the margin=8 candidate buffer in the Gram-select/exact-refine path is an undocumented safety limit with no runtime guard. Exact on every realistic cloud (rel 0.000e+00 against float64 at offsets to 1e6 and on real gpt2 states) but it silently degrades once d2_typ/||x||^2 < ~1e-13, with no assertion or fallback at that boundary.

CODE: the cache and non-cache paths score different populations -- the cache keeps every token of each document while collect_hidden_states subsamples at most 10 tokens per document -- so the same config yields two different estimators.

CODE: single-layer mode reads cache.get_hidden_states(layer_idx=-1), which for HF causal LMs is the POST-final-norm entry rather than the last block output; well defined, but not 'layer N' in the sense the layerwise list uses.

ESTIMATOR (not a defect, a caveat): at the shipped k=20 the estimate truncates at high true dimension -- d-ball medians run -4.4% at d=10 and -18.4% at d=20 -- so lid_mean compresses differences between high-dimensional models.
fix: The docstring defect is closed and the attribution is now correct (Ma et al. 2018 Eq. (4), +5.2632% over Levina-Bickel, +11.1111% over the (k-2) form -- both figures verified numerically). Remaining: 1) decide and DOCUMENT the duplicate policy and report the dropped count outside a _meta_ key, since it shifts lid_mean by +1.01% on the shipped gpt2 path. 2) Add a guard that widens the candidate margin (or falls back to a blockwise cdist) when the clamped Gram d2 goes negative, plus a regression test at offset 1e7. 3) Standardise token sampling across the cache and non-cache paths. 4) Residualise lid_mean on d_model before it is used as beyond-scale evidence; do NOT divide by sqrt(d), which over-corrects to rho = -0.735. NORMALIZED-VARIANT AXIS (measured 2026-09-04): the registered twin lid_mean/log(d_model) is RED. Its stated mechanism -- 'LID over a d-dimensional cloud carries a log(d) term' -- is refuted by the same invariance already recorded above: the Ma et al. estimator returns a bit-identical value under isometric embedding (LID 9.7467 at ambient d = 64...4096 on a fixed 10-dimensional cloud), so the estimator has no log(d) term and the divisor alone drives that twin from 2.3436 to 1.1718 across the same range. On the 66-model archive the twin does flatten the two headline axes (+0.502/+0.425 -> +0.029/+0.082) but it converts a null vocabulary association into a significant one: rho(vocab) -0.182 (p = 0.14) -> -0.408 (p = 6.8e-04), because log(d_model) itself carries rho = +0.314 with vocab. And the association it exists to remove is configuration-dependent: over 13 freshly run models at the SHIPPED default (num_samples 50, layerwise false) raw lid_mean has rho(d_model) = +0.022, with the twin at -0.115. Fit without mechanism, and it trades a width term for a vocabulary term -- remove the registration and residualise instead, as item 4 above already recommends.
